items.speaker: other
items.question: I'm on the yearly Plus, it renewed on the fifteenth of January, and I've only got the one camera now so Basic would do me. If I switch down today, the seventh of October, do I get anything back for the rest of the year?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: Two documents. The refund policy gives the rule for moving to a cheaper plan during an annual term: a credit of (old annual price - new annual price) / 12 for each FULL month remaining, added as account credit and not paid back to the card. The billing guide gives the prices: Keep Plus $130 a year, Keep Basic $60 a year (Basic covers one camera, which is what she has). The term runs from 15 January 2026 to 15 January 2027; on 7 October the full months left are 15 October to 15 November, to 15 December and to 15 January: three. (130 - 60) / 12 x 3 = $17.50 of account credit. The billing guide's 'no credit for the current month' is the rule for MONTHLY plans and does not apply. Counting four months gives $23.33.

required_facts.text: Three full months remain, so the credit is (130 - 60) / 12 x 3 = $17.50.
It is added as account credit against future charges, not paid back to the card.

optional_facts.text: Keep Basic is $60 a year and covers one camera.

forbidden_claims.text: Applies the monthly-plan rule and says there is no credit.
Counts four months remaining.
Refunds the whole price difference, or the months already used.
Uses the Pro and Plus prices.
Says the money goes back to her card.
Treats it as a refund request outside the 30-day window and refuses.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person
acceptable_inference: Mentioning that Basic keeps 14 days of clips instead of 30.

inputs.full_months_remaining: stated in the question (renewed 15 January, today 7 October: 3)

items.question: is she right? what does roam link come to for the month for both cameras, overage included

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The usage is said on the call; the rule is in the billing guide. Roam Link is $5 per camera per month: $10 for two. Each camera includes 3 GB and allowances are NOT shared, so the customer's pooling (5.9 GB against 6) is wrong. The first camera (0.8 GB) is under. The second (5.1 GB) is 2.1 GB over, and a part GB is rounded up to a whole one: 3 GB at $4 = $12. Roam Link for the month: $10 + $12 = $22. So she is not right: there is $12 of extra data.

required_facts.text: Allowances are per camera and not shared, so the second camera is 2.1 GB over.
The 2.1 GB over is billed as 3 GB at $4: $12 of extra data.

optional_facts.text: With the $5 monthly fee for each of the two cameras the Roam Link total is $22.

forbidden_claims.text: Agrees with the customer that pooling the two allowances leaves nothing extra to pay.
Bills the overage without rounding the part gigabyte up.
Rounds the overage down to 2 GB.
Pools the allowance and still bills an overage on a shared figure.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent asking privately mid-call; the answer advises the agent and may give words to say
acceptable_inference: Giving words to say that explain why the two allowances cannot be added together.

items.question: I'm in Boston, and I put the order through at twenty to two this afternoon with the next-day delivery. It's Friday the sixteenth today, so that's on my doorstep tomorrow, right?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The shipping policy: Next Business Day delivery applies when the order is placed by 1:00 pm CENTRAL. Boston is on Eastern time, one hour ahead, so 1:40 pm there is 12:40 pm Central and the order made the cut-off. The method is next BUSINESS day, and the day after Friday 16 October 2026 is a Saturday, so the estimate is Monday 19 October, not tomorrow. It is an estimate: no delivery date is guaranteed on any method; if it does arrive late the $29.00 shipping charge is refunded automatically. Saying the cut-off was missed (which would give Tuesday) or agreeing to Saturday are the mistakes.

required_facts.text: The order made the 1:00 pm Central cut-off, and the next business day after Friday is Monday 19 October.

optional_facts.text: No delivery date is guaranteed; it is an estimate.
If a Next Business Day order arrives late, its $29.00 shipping charge is refunded automatically.

forbidden_claims.text: Says the order missed the cut-off, reading 1:40 pm as Central time.
Agrees that it will arrive tomorrow, Saturday.
Guarantees or promises the delivery day.
Promises compensation beyond the automatic refund of the shipping charge.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person
acceptable_inference: Saying the parcel travels with Halberd Air.

calculation_oracle.expression: next business day after date(2026-10-16), order placed 13:40 Eastern = 12:40 Central, before the 13:00 Central cut-off

inputs.ordered_at: stated in the question (1:40 pm in Boston, Friday 16 October)
inputs.time_zone: general knowledge (Eastern is one hour ahead of Central)

items.speaker: other
items.question: I've only just found your reset e-mail, it had gone into my junk folder. It says it was sent at ten to three, and it's twenty-five past three now. Can I still use that link?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The recovery procedure has several clocks and only one of them is the link's. A reset link expires 30 minutes after it is sent: sent at 2:50, it stopped working at 3:20, five minutes ago. So no; the agent sends a fresh one (up to 5 can be sent in 24 hours) and asks the customer to use it straight away. The 10 minutes is the life of a step-up code, the 15 minutes is the lock after failed sign-ins, the 5 minutes is how long the e-mail can take to arrive, and the 7 days and 72 hours belong to a changed login e-mail.

required_facts.text: A reset link expires 30 minutes after it is sent, so this one ran out at 3:20.

optional_facts.text: A new reset e-mail can be sent; no more than 5 go to one account in 24 hours.
The e-mail can take up to 5 minutes to arrive and may land in junk.

forbidden_claims.text: Says the link is still good.
Gives another clock's length as the link's life.
Offers to set or read out a password instead.

oracle.expected_role: Tier 1 support agent speaking to the customer on the call, first person
acceptable_inference: Offering to send a new link now and stay on the line while it arrives.
